index.definition: Sum of vote-weighted z-scores of eight non-nested substance-use rates: mj, alc, cig, iem, coc, opin, met, hal. Each z-score uses the vote-weighted mean and the vote-weighted standard deviation. A region at the vote-weighted mean on every rate scores 0. One standard deviation above the mean on every rate scores 8.

iem.label: Past-month illicit drugs other than marijuana

excluded_from_index.ill: Past-month illicit drug use includes marijuana.
excluded_from_index.tob: Past-month tobacco product use includes cigarettes.
excluded_from_index.binge: Past-month binge alcohol is the heavy-drinking part of alcohol use, not a second substance.
excluded_from_index.pnr: Past-year pain reliever misuse is inside past-year opioid misuse.
excluded_from_index.her: Past-year heroin is published for ages 18 or older, not 12 or older.
excluded_from_index.ualc: Underage alcohol repeats alcohol on ages 12–20.
excluded_from_index.ubinge: Underage binge repeats binge alcohol on ages 12–20.
excluded_from_index.ucig: Underage cigarettes repeat cigarettes on ages 12–20.
excluded_from_index.utob: Underage tobacco repeats tobacco products on ages 12–20.

not_at_substate: Past-month cocaine. The substate file has past-year cocaine (COCYR) only.
Past-month heroin. The substate file has past-year heroin (HERYR), ages 18 or older.
Past-month methamphetamine. The substate file has past-year methamphetamine (METAMYR).
Past-month hallucinogens. The substate file has past-year hallucinogens (HALLUYR).
Past-month opioid misuse. The substate file has past-year opioid misuse (OPINMYR).
Past-month pain reliever misuse. The substate file has past-year pain reliever misuse (PNRNMYR).
Heavy alcohol use as its own field. Binge alcohol in the past month (BNGDRK) is the intensity measure SAMHSA published. There is no separate heavy-drinking column.
Nicotine vaping as its own rate. Tobacco product use in the past month (TOBMON) is the tobacco field. A separate vaping outcome is not among the 39.
Fentanyl, inhalants, LSD, PCP, and crack as their own substate rates. They are not among the 39 outcomes.
